bull_bear.body:
- Two FSSAI-licensed and BIS-compliant beverage manufacturing facilities in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, giving an established co-packing footprint for brand owners
- High-capacity lines — water bottling at 150 bottles per minute and juice packaging at 180 containers per minute — supporting large-brand volume requirements
- Established relationship with a reputed brand owner: co-packing of non-carbonated water and juice products for Tata Consumer Products Limited
- Product-capability widening through the newly commissioned Jelly Pouch Production Line (160 containers per minute) at Jangaon
- Positioned in the outsourced contract-manufacturing/co-packing segment, which the Company describes as a key enabler for leading beverage brands expanding market presence
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration / dependence on key customers and contract manufacturing arrangements — Explicitly flagged in MD&A Risks and Concerns and again as a threat. As a co-packer the Company's volumes sit with a handful of brand owners — the AR names only Tata Consumer Products Limited as a customer for its non-carbonated water and juice work, so loss or re-tendering of one contract would hit a large share of revenue.
- Raw material and packaging material price fluctuations — Listed both as a risk and as a threat; input and packaging costs move independently of contract pricing, and the Company attributes part of FY26's profitability decline to higher operating costs.
- Liquidity and debt-servicing risk — Liquidity risk is named in MD&A Risks and Concerns. The corporate-governance annexure records repeated one-day delays in principal and interest payments on Axis Bank Ltd term loans in nearly every month of FY 2025-26, plus unpaid Provident Fund and Employee State Insurance dues, and the Current Ratio fell to 0.43 from 1.36 — all consistent with tight liquidity.
- Profitability / margin erosion and loss-making operations — MD&A attributes the year's decline to higher operating costs, employee expenses and exceptional items; Operating Profit Margin turned negative (-11.14% vs 8.06%), Net Profit Margin fell to -16.34%, RONW to (14.64%) from (1.61%), and the Interest Coverage Ratio is cited as having declined significantly owing to losses incurred.
- Intense competition in contract manufacturing and beverage packaging — Flagged as a threat. Co-packing is a low-differentiation, capacity-led business, so competing lines constrain the pricing the Company can hold with brand owners.
- Regulatory and food-safety compliance risk — Named in both Risks and Concerns and Threats — compliance requirements relating to food safety and quality standards. The Company's licence to operate rests on FSSAI licensing and BIS compliance at both facilities.
- Changing consumer preferences and supply-chain disruption — Explicitly flagged in Risks and Concerns as able to impact business performance — a shift away from the packaged water and fruit-juice formats the lines are configured for would strand capacity.
- Economic uncertainty and inflationary pressure on operating margins — Listed as a threat and repeated in Risks and Concerns; inflation raises employee and operating costs that the Company has not been able to pass through, as seen in FY26.

outlook.body: ABVL operates two manufacturing facilities — Kallem, Jangaon (Telangana) and Annadevarapeta, Kovvur (Andhra Pradesh) — both FSSAI licensed and BIS compliant, running water bottling lines of 150 bottles per minute and juice packaging lines of 180 containers per minute. The single expansion event of FY 2025-26 was the commissioning of a new Jelly Pouch Production Line with a capacity of 160 containers per minute at the Jangaon facility, which the Company says enhances its production capabilities and strengthens its position in the beverage packaging industry. Management states that this newly commissioned line, together with the existing high-capacity beverage packaging infrastructure, is expected to support future growth, and lists expansion of production capacities and product diversification among its opportunities; beyond that the Company names no further project, no commissioning timeline and no rupee capex quantum anywhere in the narrative chapters. Related-party disclosures record the purchase of land and a constructed godown from two related parties during FY 2025-26, but the annual report does not describe these as part of a named expansion project.

outlook.body:
- Indian beverage industry growth driven by rising consumer demand for packaged beverages, increasing health consciousness, urbanization and growing preference for quality-assured products
- Outlook for the Indian beverage industry remains positive, supported by increasing consumer demand, expanding distribution networks and growing preference for branded packaged beverages
- Increasing outsourcing of manufacturing and packaging activities by leading FMCG and beverage companies — contract manufacturing/co-packing has emerged as a key enabler for brands to expand market presence efficiently
- Rising consumer preference for hygienically packed beverages and growing demand for packaged drinking water, fruit juices and ready-to-consume beverages
- Margin pressure from higher operating costs, employee expenses and exceptional items recognised during the year; fluctuations in raw material and packaging material costs and inflationary pressures are flagged as threats to operating margins
- Long-term growth prospects in the Indian food and beverage sector

The corporate-governance annexure records repeated one-day delays in principal and interest payments on Axis Bank Ltd term loans in nearly every month of FY 2025-26, plus unpaid Provident Fund and Employee State Insurance dues, and the Current Ratio fell to 0.43 from 1.36 — all consistent with tight liquidity.
- Profitability / margin erosion and loss-making operations — MD&A attributes the year's decline to higher operating costs, employee expenses and exceptional items; Operating Profit Margin turned negative (-11.14% vs 8.06%), Net Profit Margin fell to -16.34%, RONW to (14.64%) from (1.61%), and the Interest Coverage Ratio is cited as having declined significantly owing to losses incurred.
- Intense competition in contract manufacturing and beverage packaging — Flagged as a threat. Co-packing is a low-differentiation, capacity-led business, so competing lines constrain the pricing the Company can hold with brand owners.
- Regulatory and food-safety compliance risk — Named in both Risks and Concerns and Threats — compliance requirements relating to food safety and quality standards. The Company's licence to operate rests on FSSAI licensing and BIS compliance at both facilities.
- Changing consumer preferences and supply-chain disruption — Explicitly flagged in Risks and Concerns as able to impact business performance — a shift away from the packaged water and fruit-juice formats the lines are configured for would strand capacity.
- Economic uncertainty and inflationary pressure on operating margins — Listed as a threat and repeated in Risks and Concerns; inflation raises employee and operating costs that the Company has not been able to pass through, as seen in FY26.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen relationships with existing brand-owner customers in the co-packing business
- Improve operational efficiencies and enhance capacity utilization across the two facilities
- Expand product offerings — product diversification alongside expansion of production capacities
- Leverage the newly commissioned Jelly Pouch Production Line and existing high-capacity beverage packaging infrastructure to support future growth
- Improve profitability after the loss-making year, with management committed to generating long-term value for stakeholders
- Attract and retain talent, keeping employees engaged, …

hero.oneLiner: Arunjyoti Bio Ventures Limited is a BSE-listed beverage co-packing and packaging company providing end-to-end manufacturing, processing, filling and packaging solutions to reputed consumer brands in the packaged drinking water and fruit-based beverage segments.
